Given two $n\times n$ matrices $M$ and $N,$ we have

$$
det(MN)=det(M)\cdot det(N).
$$

In our case, this gives

$$
det(K)=det[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 2 \\ -3 & 1 & -7 \\ 4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot det[\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

We can compute the required determinants as follows:

- For the first determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion down the $2$nd column.

- For the second determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion across the $3$rd row.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(K) & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 2 \\ -3 & 1 & -7 \\ 4 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 6 \\ 3 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}|\cdot (-3)(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(15-8)\cdot (-3)(8-9) \\  & =7\cdot 3 \\  & =21.\end{aligned}
$$
